indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.3.3.1 Show understanding of ecosystem, interdependency of organisms in an ecosystem and appreciate the interactions
indicator.objective: Know how various organisms are adapted to survive in their habitat

skills.description: Define habitat as the natural home of a plant or animal.
Identify examples of habitats (e.g. water, land, trees, soil).
Explain simply that adaptation means features that help an organism survive in its habitat.
Describe how specific animals are adapted to their habitat (e.g. fish have gills and fins for water; birds have wings for flying; camels have humps for dry areas).
Describe how specific plants are adapted to their habitat (e.g. cacti have spines to reduce water loss; water lilies have flat leaves to float).
Explain why adaptation is important for survival (e.g. finding food, escaping danger).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: All animals can live in any habitat.
Adaptation means the animal changes its body instantly.
Plants do not need to adapt.
A habitat is just any place.

questions.stem: What is a habitat?
options: The natural home of a plant or animal
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal.
questions.misconception: A habitat is just any place.

questions.stem: Which of these best describes a habitat?
options: A place where an organism lives naturally
A place where people go to shop
hints: It is about where living things live.
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home where an organism lives.

questions.stem: What is a habitat?
answer: the natural home of a plant or animal
the home of a living thing
where an organism lives naturally
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal.
questions.misconception: A habitat is just any place.

questions.stem: Which of these is a habitat for fish?
questions.explanation: Water is the habitat for fish. They are adapted to live in water.

questions.stem: Which of these is a habitat for a bird?
questions.explanation: Trees are a common habitat for many birds.

questions.stem: Name two examples of habitats.
answer: water and land
land and trees
water and trees
soil and water
hints: One is wet, one is dry.
questions.explanation: Examples of habitats include water, land, trees and soil.

questions.stem: What does adaptation mean?
options: Features that help an organism survive in its habitat
hints: It helps the organism live in its home.
questions.explanation: Adaptation means the features that help an organism survive in its habitat.
questions.misconception: Adaptation means the animal changes its body instantly.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains adaptation?
options: Adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat
Adaptation is when an animal changes colour for fun
Adaptation is the food an animal eats
Adaptation is the sound an animal makes
hints: It helps the organism live in its home.
questions.explanation: Adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat.
questions.misconception: Adaptation is not related to survival.

questions.stem: What is adaptation?
answer: features that help an organism survive in its habitat
special features that help living things survive
characteristics that help organisms live in their environment
questions.explanation: Adaptation refers to features that help an organism survive in its habitat.
questions.misconception: Adaptation means the animal changes instantly.

questions.stem: How is a fish adapted to live in water?
options: It has gills to breathe in water and fins to swim
It has lungs to breathe air
questions.explanation: Fish are adapted to water with gills for breathing and fins for swimming.
questions.misconception: Fish have lungs for breathing air.

questions.stem: How is a camel adapted to live in a dry desert?
options: It has a hump that stores fat for energy
hints: The hump helps it survive without much food and water.
questions.explanation: A camel has a hump that stores fat, helping it survive in dry desert conditions.

questions.stem: Describe one adaptation that helps a bird survive in its habitat.
answer: wings for flying to find food
beak for eating
feathers for warmth
wings to escape danger
questions.explanation: Birds have wings for flying, which helps them find food and escape danger.

questions.stem: A fish is taken out of water and placed on land. It soon dies. Why?
options: It cannot get oxygen from the air using its gills
It does not like the colour of the ground
hints: Fish use gills to breathe in water.
Gills do not work well in air.
questions.explanation: Fish are adapted to breathe oxygen dissolved in water using gills. On land, their gills cannot get enough oxygen from the air, so they die.

questions.stem: How is a cactus adapted to live in a dry area?
options: It has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss
It has large flat leaves to catch sunlight
It has many roots that grow above the ground
questions.explanation: A cactus has spines instead of leaves, which reduces water loss and helps it survive in dry areas.

questions.stem: Describe one adaptation that helps a water lily survive in water.
answer: it has flat leaves that float on water
its leaves float on the water surface
it has long stems that reach the surface
questions.explanation: Water lilies have flat leaves that float on the water surface, helping them get sunlight.

questions.stem: Draw a simple diagram of a cactus and a water lily. Label one adaptation of each that helps it survive in its habitat. Write one sentence explaining each adaptation.

criteria.description: Drew a recognizable cactus and water lily
Labeled one adaptation of the cactus (e.g. spines)
Labeled one adaptation of the water lily (e.g. flat floating leaves)
Explained how the cactus adaptation helps it survive
Explained how the water lily adaptation helps it survive

hints: Cacti have spines and thick stems.
Water lilies have flat leaves that float.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Plants do not need to adapt.

questions.stem: Why is adaptation important for animals?
options: It helps them survive in their habitat
hints: Think about finding food and escaping danger.
questions.explanation: Adaptation is important because it helps animals survive in their habitat.

questions.stem: A bird has a sharp beak for eating insects. Why is this adaptation important?
options: It helps the bird find and eat food
It helps the bird change colour
hints: A sharp beak helps with food.
questions.explanation: A sharp beak helps the bird catch and eat insects, which is important for its survival.

questions.stem: Why do living things need adaptations?
answer: to survive in their habitat
to find food and escape danger
to live successfully in their environment
questions.explanation: Living things need adaptations to survive in their habitat, find food and escape danger.

questions.stem: In groups, design and make a simple model of a habitat for a named animal (e.g. fish in a pond, bird in a tree). Your model should show at least two features that help the animal survive in that habitat. Present your model to the class and explain the adaptations.

criteria.description: Designed a model of a habitat for a named animal
Showed at least two features that help the animal survive
Explained the adaptations clearly to the class

hints: Choose an animal and its habitat.
Think about what helps it live there (e.g. gills, wings, roots).
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: All animals can live in any habitat.
